newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish mostly lower, off lows.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish mostly lower, off lows.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly lower but above session lows, with the yen posting hety losses on the day.
Turnover picked up slightly again near the close, when one fund was seen selling marks and buying sterling. It also bought 500 September Canadian dollars, floor brokers said.
"Other than that, it (close) was quiet," said a broker.

The yen's sharp drop dragged other units down as well, as the Japanese unit succumbed to a confluence of factors. Those included technicals, interest-rate spreads, crosses, and spillover from jitters afflicting Southeast Asian currencies.

September yen before midday skidded below several key levels, pummelled by large fund sales including one that sold some 2,000 contracts near $0.008600. That hit sellstops as sellers piled in anticipation of a more prolonged decline, floor brokers said.
"It was fund selling, and it was happening very quickly, (it was) very choppy," said another floor broker. "I think it's not over yet. I think they're (yen) going to drop again."
But the unit finally managed to respect a support zone.
"They got to a critical level, and they just bounced," said a technician of the $0.008508 area, roughly 118.05 spot.
"But I think we'll see 120.00," he added.
Such a dollar rise would mean September yen could visit the $0.008370 level.

Yen also continued under pressure from overnight after Indonesia effectively floated its currency, which underscored concerns that the recent tumble in other Southeast Asian currencies could spread and damage the yen, especially if Japanese exports suffer or simply by Japan's proximity to those countries.
"It (yen) should be a safe-haven...but Japan could be called upon to help out," said one analyst.
Marks stayed in the minus column but regained some ground as ideas spread that German rates might rise soon to fend off inflation and one persistent EMU delay talk.
Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said the Bundesbank wants to keep full leeway on its repo rate.
Earlier, Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber was quoted as saying it would be best to delay Eurpena union if France and Germany did not respect Maastricht criteria to the letter.

Yen off $0.000177 at $0.008510, marks off $0.0018 at $0.5443, Swiss fr fell $0.0031 to $0.6612, pound up $0.0050 to $1.5870, Cdollar up $0.0011 at $0.7202, Adollar off $0.0027 to $0.7417, Mex peso up $0.000525 to $0.127325. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
